model: RVL-001 original white with RVL-003 Remote and RVL-004 Nunchuk

sources.verified: RVL-001 front/rear and GameCube compartment arrangements. Rear exhaust has a five-by-five field; rear USB sockets form a close pair.
sources.scope: Original RVL-001 body diagrams; this later manual printing does not define a launch-bundle wrist-strap revision.

sources.verified: Original RVL-003 Remote, three columns by six rows of speaker holes, battery-compartment SYNC control and housing strap attachment.
sources.scope: Body details only. The illustrated RVL-018A strap and RVL-022 jacket are not added to this model.

sources.verified: Original white Remote front and side photograph corroborates eighteen graded-size speaker holes.
Early 0.6 mm and replacement 1 mm strap cords differ.
sources.scope: Variant check only; no later strap revision is silently substituted.

exterior_review.before: Overlong 70.3 mm SD cover, short/wide controls, and Wii wordmark kept horizontal after the console was laid down.
exterior_review.after: Cover width fitted to 61.5 mm, narrower/taller power/reset/eject caps with corresponding holes, and the wordmark rotated with the original faceplate.
exterior_review.basis: Official front diagram normalized by the 157 mm axis; local dimensions and font shapes remain estimates. Main slot location and control ordering retained.

exterior_review.before: Ten tall exhaust slits, 17 mm USB center spacing and a pale AV connector surround.
exterior_review.after: Twenty-five square exhaust cells, 8.5 mm USB center spacing, dark AV surround and orange sensor-bar keying.
exterior_review.basis: Opening topology and color roles are documented; cell size 6.2 mm, pitch 6.8 mm, USB spacing and numerical RGB values are diagram fits. Existing fan center is retained.

exterior_review.finding: Side, controller-port order with port 1 nearest the front, and memory slots behind the controller bank agree with the manual. Covers are hidden for comparison; exact local slot and hinge dimensions remain unmeasured.

exterior_review.before: Main controls were about 7-10 mm too low in the photograph fit; twenty-one speaker holes; numerical player marks below the lamps; no bottom Wii wordmark.
exterior_review.after: Repositioned key/plunger/contact stacks, speaker and lamps; eighteen graded holes; one-to-four dot patterns above the lamps and bottom Wii lettering.
exterior_review.basis: Original product photograph normalized to 36.2 x 148 mm. All local positions, hole sizes and the replacement font remain fitted approximations; the schematic EEPROM package moves 3 mm within the board to clear the corrected speaker.

exterior_review.finding: Add the documented red SYNC button with a schematic PCB-mounted switch and an integral lanyard passage. No strap or jacket added.
Public gross console envelope retained. Local longitudinal Remote rear curvature, B-trigger contour and detailed console molding have not been measured and remain reconstruction limits.

model_parameters_not_factory_dimensions.sync_and_strap_geometry: Estimated local placement and package/bridge dimensions; not a Nintendo switch or molding drawing.

remote_front_calibration.coordinate_rule: local x=(pixel x-154.5)*36.2/67; local y=(149-pixel y)*148/270. Most target coordinates rounded to 0.5 mm; pixel selections and perspective are not manufacturing tolerances.
remote_front_calibration.wordmark_note: Existing CAD font used; original typeface is not claimed.

limitations: No hardware sample, factory connector drawing or molding tolerance data was measured.
The source printing includes later accessories; only the explicitly identified original console and Remote body features are used.
The existing internal PCB and mechanism layout remains schematic; valid fit does not establish electrical or mechanical operation.
Official reference images remain local and are not redistributed.
